module_title: MS Excel - Formula Errors, VLOOKUP, and Logical Functions
introduction: Tailored for SSC CGL Tier-2 (Mains) and technical IT Officer exams, this advanced module breaks down the meaning behind various Excel 'Error Codes', logic-based functions (IF), and advanced data retrieval tools like VLOOKUP.

core_concepts.title: Logical Function: IF
core_concepts.description:
Syntax: `=IF(Condition, Value_if_True, Value_if_False)` 
Excel's most powerful decision-making function. Example: `=IF(A1>33, "Pass", "Fail")`. If the score in A1 is greater than 33, it prints 'Pass'; otherwise, it prints 'Fail'.

core_concepts.title: VLOOKUP (Vertical Lookup)
core_concepts.description: An advanced function used to search for a specific piece of data within a massive database table. It searches 'Vertically' (down the first column) to find a match, and then returns data from the same row. (Note: HLOOKUP is used for horizontal row searching).

core_concepts.title: Decoding Excel Error Codes
core_concepts.description:
When a formula fails, Excel outputs a specific error code starting with a Hash (`#`):
- `#DIV/0!`: Occurs when you attempt to divide a number by zero or by a completely empty cell.
- `#NAME?`: Occurs when there is a spelling mistake in the function name (e.g., typing `=SOM()` instead of `=SUM()`).
- `#VALUE!`: Occurs when you mix incompatible data types in a calculation (e.g., trying to add 'Apple' + 5).
- `#REF!`: (Reference Error) Occurs when a cell used in a formula has been entirely deleted from the worksheet.

core_concepts.title: Text Functions
core_concepts.description:
- `=CONCATENATE(A1, B1)`: Used to merge or join the text of two or more separate cells into one single cell (e.g., joining First Name and Last Name).
- `=LEN(A1)`: Calculates the total 'Length' of a cell (i.e., counts exactly how many characters and spaces are inside the cell).

important_entities.name: BODMAS / PEMDAS Execution
important_entities.significance: Excel strictly follows standard math hierarchy. It calculates Parentheses `()` first, then Exponents `^`, then Multiplication/Division `* /`, and finally Addition/Subtraction `+ -`.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A popular matching question in Mains. Remember the distinction: If the function's spelled name is wrong, it's `#NAME?`. If the name is correct, but you put bad data (like text instead of numbers) inside the formula, it's `#VALUE!`.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: The ##### Display is NOT an Error
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: If a cell suddenly displays a row of hashes (e.g., `######`), aspirants assume the formula broke. It hasn't! This simply means the number inside the cell is physically too wide to fit within the current column width. Just double-click the column edge to widen it.

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Instead of writing the long `=CONCATENATE(A1, B1)` function, you can simply use the `&` symbol to join text: `=A1&B1` does the exact same thing instantly.

exam_strategy_tips: In Tier-2 analytical exams, memorize the exact definitions of `#DIV/0!` and `#REF!`. Also, always remember that the 'V' in VLOOKUP strictly stands for 'Vertical'.
